answer: Natural-material token fingerprinting ties each identity to a token cut from cedar grown on an island grove, with a jade inlay carrying a laser-etched serial. At signup, the applicant presents the token and its cedar-grain pattern is scanned and hashed; the hash must match the registry, and one token backs one identity. Forging 100 identities needs 100 tokens at $125 each, $12,500 in total.
